hypotheses.confidence_note: Conditional local two-second prototype, not a verified trajectory or world-safety assertion. Ego initially moves at the supplied 8.906 m/s. Continue in the present lane with a mild speed-reduction preference; do not stop for a crossing-warning sign alone. The oncoming SUV and left-side cones are retained. The cone row is represented by a conservative aggregate BODY box, not an individual vehicle. Road geometry and depths are approximate visual hypotheses, not calibrated ground-plane measurements. Side parking areas, garage interiors, distant parked vehicles and rear traffic outside the finite local domain are excluded only under the explicit no-entry condition. No independent dynamics/collision verification or prefix simulation has been performed here; the narrow passing clearance must be checked with the supplied full-body limits and unchanged safety margin.

premises.statement: The local prototype domain is the finite patch x=[-22,32], y=[-6,9] in fixed reference axes. The road polygon is the modeled continuous paved subset used for ego travel, including the present footprint and approximately 18 m of intended forward travel. Adopt no new unobserved pedestrian, cyclist, vehicle or other entrant into this domain during [0,2]. Distant vehicles beyond its forward boundary, parking-lot traffic, garage interiors and traffic farther behind are not asserted absent; their entry is excluded conditionally. All observed obstacles identified within or immediately threatening the modeled route are retained as the oncoming SUV and cone-row aggregate. This scope is falsified by an entrant or motion outside the separately stated movement conditions.

The dark SUV visible in the reference front image is modeled as a 4.8 m long, 1.95 m wide rectangular BODY facing approximately opposite ego. These are conditional passenger-SUV dimension priors, not measured dimensions. Its native reference BODY center is estimated at (7.4,3.65). At yaw pi its initial corners lie at x=5.0 or 9.8 and y=2.675 or 4.625, enclosed by both source alternatives.

Conditional on the observed straight oncoming approach continuing without a turn or lane crossing: adopted absolute longitudinal velocity is in [-8,-6] m/s, with fixed lateral center and yaw pi. The adverse retained range is vx in [-10,-6] m/s, cumulative lateral displacement within +/-0.15 m and yaw within pi +/-0.025 rad. The adverse BODY half-extents are bounded by 2.425 m longitudinally and 1.035 m laterally. Whole-interval rectangles include every initial and intermediate BODY pose under these bounds. Their model residual excludes the direct-observation alignment residual.

The visible cones along the left curb in front frame 003 are modeled jointly by an enclosing 11 m by 0.7 m ground BODY box centered at reference coordinates (12,5.8), yaw zero. This aggregate deliberately fills the gaps between cones. Position at the actual capture offset -0.5 s is estimated after supplied ego-pose compensation. Adopt stationary cones over [-0.5,2]; the adverse condition allows translation at at most 0.1 m/s, no rotation, at most 0.05 m before reference and 0.2 m after reference. This supplies the past alignment bound as well as future coverage; the 0.2 m alignment residual additionally covers estimating the aggregate position. No cone falls or is displaced beyond this declared bound.

Approximate straight continuous pavement is inferred from the visible curb/sidewalk edges, double-yellow center marking and right dashed marking in the reference front image, with near-rear pavement supported by the rear image at offset -0.0248458 s and supplied ego history. A conservative interior paved patch spans x=[-6,28], y=[-4.5,7]. Left pavement extends beyond the opposing lane; right pavement extends beyond the dashed marking but not onto sidewalk. The finite longitudinal cuts are modeling boundaries, not physical road ends. A 0.4 m noncalibrated road-boundary residual is retained. Perspective and the SUV size prior supply approximate metric scale; no certified ground plane is claimed.

anchors.rationale: The individually observed dark SUV is assigned a typical approximately 1.95 m passenger-SUV body width; this is a falsifiable category prior rather than known vehicle specification.
Its visible SUV body and side extent support using a conditional 4.8 m length, matching the native BODY hypothesis.

metric_scale_support.metric_reasoning: The reference SUV's large image extent, visible front and receding side support a body center several metres ahead and roughly one opposing-lane offset left. Comparing its assumed 1.95 m width and 4.8 m length with perspective-converging lane markings gives the native center estimate (7.4,3.65). The supplied camera axes establish left/right and forward orientation, not certified depth. Extending the visually straight curb and pavement boundaries at this approximate scale yields the stated local road patch; the cone row is estimated from its actual historical image with supplied ego displacement. All distances and residuals remain model-metric hypotheses conditional on these body-size and pavement assumptions.
